bullets.title: ISM Manufacturing solid but prices-paid collapse; ADP payrolls softer ahead of NFP
bullets.body: ISM Manufacturing came in at 53.3 in June (down from 54.0 in May), with new orders slipping to 56.0 from 56.8 — but prices-paid dropped sharply to 73.0 from 82.1, the largest single-month decline since July 2022. ADP private payrolls printed 98K vs. consensus 110-120K. JPM forecasts Friday NFP at 125K (vs. Street 115K) with 4.3% unemployment; a 22V survey found 52% of investors expect a risk-on reaction and 60% expect a beat vs. sell-side consensus.

bullets.title: Fed Chair Warsh leans dovish on AI productivity; signals move away from dot plot
bullets.body: Warsh at ECB Sintra cited 'high 2s' productivity growth over the past four quarters and flagged AI's potential 'huge implications for monetary policy,' sending long-end Treasury yields up ~6bp. He also noted inflation expectations and risks have declined over the past four weeks, and indicated the Fed wants to eliminate the dot plot and move away from forward guidance. Former BoE Governor Mervyn King to co-chair a new communications task force, with details likely next week.

bullets.title: Citi raises S&P 500 year-end target to 8,100; above-consensus earnings of $350/$400 for '26/'27
bullets.body: Citi lifted its S&P 500 base case to 8,100, driven by above-consensus EPS estimates of $350 in 2026 and $400 in 2027. The firm expects recent outperformance in semis and hardware to broaden in 2H, sees Fed rate hike fears as overblown, and notes that Iran conflict wind-down supports lower oil. Q2 earnings season fundamentals per FactSet: 12.1% revenue growth, 22.0% earnings growth, 14.1% margins.

bullets.title: Semiconductor selloff 6-11% on META neocloud news — JPM calls it positioning, not a demand shift
bullets.body: Semis fell 6.3% and memory dropped ~11% (MU -10.6%) after Bloomberg reported META is building a cloud business to sell excess AI compute. JPM views the selloff as de-grossing and positioning rather than a fundamental demand shift, maintaining a tactical bullish stance into earnings. DA Davidson flags NBIS (META >50% of backlog) and CRWV (META ~33%) as most exposed negatives; sees MU, NVDA, and GOOGL as relatively unscathed.

bullets.title: META +8.8% on 'Meta Compute' cloud plan — bulls see $20B+ ARR, bears see capex ROI desperation
bullets.body: META surged ~9% after Bloomberg reported it is building 'Meta Compute' to sell excess AI capacity and model access (AWS Bedrock-style), monetizing its ~2 GW/'26 and ~3.5 GW/'27 owned capacity ramp. Morgan Stanley sees each 250 MW leased at $40/W generating ~$3 EPS accretion in '28 (~8% upside). KeyBanc sees a potential $20B+ ARR opportunity. Oppenheimer takes the contrarian view, arguing excess capacity signals advertising growth is slowing and META has failed to launch a competitive frontier LLM.

bullets.title: LLM token demand re-accelerating sharply: June volumes +70% MoM, 20x YoY
bullets.body: JPM's afternoon briefing cited June LLM token volumes up 70% MoM and 20x YoY, with spending up 70% MoM and 16x YoY. GPU rental prices rose across all tiers — B200s trading at ~2x H100s, H100s at ~1.7x A100s. DRAM spot prices are up 8x YoY after a third consecutive monthly gain. The data point supports continued AI infrastructure demand even as the META neocloud story creates near-term confusion in the semiconductor tape.

bullets.title: Hedge funds record Q2 L/S performance, then rotated out of TMT into Cyclicals in June
bullets.body: Global fundamental L/S managers posted record-breaking quarterly performance in Q2 2026, but hedge funds net sold global equities for the first time in three months in June, led by short sales. Every region except North America was net sold. Gross and net leverage fell, led by US and Asia L/S managers, and sector rotation moved out of Info Tech/Comm Services into Cyclicals in US portfolios.

bullets.title: JPM adds Healthcare as low-correlation long; midterm seasonality sets up Q3 outperformance
bullets.body: JPM's tactical framework now runs a Tech/Cyclicals barbell with Healthcare added as a low-correlated long. Separately, JPM's sector strategy notes Healthcare beats SPX by a mean +7.5 ppts (median +10.7 ppts) in midterm years, concentrated in a Q3 surge that's been positive in 7 of 9 cycles. Biotech is the strongest subsector with +15% annual outperformance in midterm years; HC Equipment & Services positioning is near 10-year lows.

bullets.title: Treasury supply wave coming: $119B mid-month ($58B 3Y, $39B 10Y, $22B 30Y); 5s/30s curve steepened through 73bp resistance
bullets.body: Treasury is set to announce $119B in mid-month supply, including $58B 3-year notes, $39B 10-year reopening, and $22B 30-year reopening. The 5s/30s curve has steepened through the 73bp resistance level off 59-62bp medium-term support; JPM sees 78-84bp as the upper bound of the summer trading range.

bullets.title: Morgan Stanley flags unsustainable semi vs. hyperscaler divergence; short interest in hyperscalers rising
bullets.body: JPM's flows note flags that semis have outperformed hyperscalers steadily since September 2025, which it views as unsustainable. Hyperscalers posted record ~100% YoY capex growth in 2026, yet their equities are flat over the past year and credit spreads have widened vs. semiconductors. Short interest in hyperscalers rose steeply in May-June 2026. The key risk is consensus expectations for sharp capex deceleration in 2027.

bullets.title: Market internals: NDX lagged SPX/RTY by 100bp; software/internet +3%, semis -6.3%, utilities -1.3%
bullets.body: NDX underperformed SPX and RTY by over 100bp on the day. Within tech, software (+3.1%) and internet (+3.1%) outperformed sharply while semis fell 6.3%. Communication services and financials were the top SPX sectors. Breadth was positive on the day — the equal-weight S&P ended higher — with momentum unwinding as a key driver. SPX closed in the 7,540-7,568 range.

bullets.title: June IPO market: SpaceX's $86B raise nearly triples the prior all-time record; Anthropic at $1.67T pre-IPO
bullets.body: June 2026 saw a record $94.99B raised across 13 IPOs, dominated by SpaceX's $86.26B IPO at a ~$1.8T valuation — nearly 3x Saudi Aramco's prior record of $29B. Cerebras ($6.4B) was the second largest. Pre-IPO sentiment: Anthropic (hired MS/GS bankers) at ~$1.67T, OpenAI (confidentially filed S-1, leaning toward 2027) at ~$1.33T. June IPOs averaged +13.1% from pricing.

bullets.title: Fed on hold thesis gains support: Morgan Stanley sees fading tariff effects, lower oil, shelter deceleration
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley argues FOMC projections overstate inflation pressures given fading tariff effects, declining oil from the Iran conflict wind-down, and shelter cost deceleration. Their view: disinflation ahead implies a lower rate path than currently priced, which is a further tailwind to equities and supports CRE/REIT recovery (names flagged: CBRE, CWK, MAA, AMT).

bullets.title: Asia capex super-cycle thesis: energy capex ($900B→$1T) dwarfs AI/semis ($380B→$420B) in 2026-27
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley argues the Asia capex super-cycle is driven equally by energy, defense, and onshoring alongside AI. Energy-related capex is expected to rise from $900B (2026) to $1T (2027), vs. AI/semis moving from $380B to $420B. Asia capital goods imports are up 33% YoY on a 3-month moving average, and semis exports are at multi-decade highs. Drivers are structural (healthy corporate balance sheets), not cyclical.

bullets.title: Korea's $3.1T mega-investment plan targets semiconductors and AI; memory capacity set to double in five years
bullets.body: South Korea launched a $3.1T Mega Investment Era through 2040: Samsung is committing W2,655T (W2,100T in semiconductors), SK Group W2,100T (W1,100T in memory, W1,000T in AI infrastructure). DRAM capacity is targeted to double in five years. Korean equities trade at 7.3x FTM P/E, -1.7 standard deviations below historical mean, despite the tech sector being the only green sector in June amid circuit breaker volatility.

bullets.title: Apple faces memory crisis: ~$200/unit cost headwind, seeking Chinese CXMT/YMTC chips despite Pentagon blacklisting
bullets.body: Apple is in talks with Chinese suppliers CXMT and YMTC for memory chips for China-market devices while lobbying the White House for support. Memory and storage prices have quadrupled over the past three quarters as production skews toward HBM for AI servers. Apple has already raised MacBook, iPad, and Mac prices 15-33%, and Counterpoint estimates a $150-$200 iPhone price increase is coming. CEO Cook called the situation 'unsustainable.'

bullets.title: IPPs (TLN -6%, VST -3.5%, CEG -4.8%) and utilities broadly sold off; BE expands Brookfield AI partnership to $25B
bullets.body: The S&P 500 Utilities Index fell 1.3% and Electric Utilities fell 1.5%, with independent power producers leading the decline — TLN -6.1%, NRG -3.6%, VST -3.5%, CEG -4.8%. Against that backdrop, Bloom Energy expanded its AI infrastructure partnership with Brookfield from $5B to $25B; Brookfield's AI Infrastructure Fund targets $100B total deployment. PJM advanced a plan to source more power to meet rising data center demand.

bullets.title: US lodging RevPAR +9.6% for week ending 6/27; World Cup adds 290bps, luxury +20.7%
bullets.body: US hotel RevPAR rose 9.6% YoY for the week of June 21-27 (ADR +9.2%, occupancy +30bps), in line with the prior week's +9.7%. The World Cup contributed 290bps; non-host city RevPAR still grew 6.8%. Luxury led at +20.7% YoY. Miami RevPAR was +51.6%, San Francisco +40.7%. Trailing 28-day RevPAR is up 8.0%. Hotel operators HLT, MAR, and HST are all tracking above consensus for 2Q.

bullets.title: Consumer staples crowding unwind; CLX margins pressured by resin costs, EL F27 guide seen as too aggressive
bullets.body: Citi flags a broad crowding unwind across staples, restaurants, and distributors as of the June 26 close. CLX F27 buyside EPS expectations are $5.85-5.90 vs. Street at $6.16, with margins pressured by resin costs in 1H. Estee Lauder's F27 guide (OSG 3-5% topline) is seen as too aggressive by bears, who expect a 1Q guide-down supported by recent China retail checks. STZ key debate: is summer 2026 peak for the stock?

bullets.title: PCE revision to trim portfolio management fee contribution by ~15bps; minimal net inflation impact
bullets.body: BEA is revising its PCE methodology for portfolio management, legal services, and software. The portfolio management contribution to 12-month core PCE may be revised down ~15bps, with legal services moving higher and software lower; net effect is a couple of bps negative. Post-revision, Core MPO PCE of 3.16% could map to underlying inflation of ~3.30% vs. current 3.36% — a modest but policy-relevant distinction.
